clue.text: Statistically manipulated a lot of people, like the old

parts.note: a mass is a large crowd of people
the old are aged, so being like them is being aged

explanation.surface: Figures were fiddled about a crowd, presented as resembling the elderly.
explanation.definitionFit: Data that have been massaged have been manipulated to look better, an idiom from statistics and accounting.

clue.text: No good at all for movie star switching parts, giving wooden displays

indicators.note: G stands for good, and having no good at all means every G is removed
the two parts of the name swap places, surname before forename

parts.note: Greta Garbo was a Swedish-born Hollywood film star

explanation.surface: Instead of a film celebrity trading roles, worthless, we get displays of wood.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping GRETA and GARBO gives GARBOGRETA; removing both Gs leaves ARBORETA.
explanation.definitionFit: Arboreta are collections of trees grown for display and study, so they are displays of wood in a playful sense.

clue.text: Show big match in which player is evaluated

parts.note: to screen a film is to show it
a Test is a major international cricket match

explanation.surface: Broadcast a major fixture where a sportsman is assessed.
explanation.walkthrough: A Test is an international cricket match between national sides.
explanation.definitionFit: A screen test is a filmed audition in which an actor, a player, is assessed for a part.

clue.text: Adapting, with changes, including an endangered species

indicators.note: including means holding something inside, here the two-letter word
with changes says the letters of the word are altered in order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Evolving with changes, which includes a species at risk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Adapting' poses as the surface verb but is the fodder for 'with changes'; 'including' then takes in the little word 'an' between P and D of the rearrangement GIANTPDA.
explanation.definitionFit: The giant panda of China is a well-known species threatened with extinction.

clue.text: Follow left-winger, running at gentle pace

definitions.note: a noun phrase for the pace itself, which the clue gives as the action

parts.note: to dog someone is to follow them closely
a Trot is a Trotskyist, a left-wing radical

explanation.surface: Shadow a socialist who is jogging slowly.
explanation.walkthrough: TROT is short for Trotskyist, a follower of Leon Trotsky.
explanation.definitionFit: A dogtrot is an easy jogging gait, the gentle pace of a trotting dog.

clue.text: Almost take out of service in protest

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter is cut

parts.note: to demob is to demobilise, release from military service

explanation.surface: Nearly discharged from the forces during a demonstration.
explanation.walkthrough: DEMOB, British slang for demobilise, loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A demo is short for demonstration, a public protest march or rally.

clue.text: Old measure restricting second kind of artist

indicators.note: restricting means hemming in, so the measure surrounds the letter

parts.note: a cubit is an ancient unit of length, about a forearm

explanation.surface: An ancient unit limiting a moment, a type of painter.
explanation.definitionFit: A cubist works in the style of Picasso and Braque, breaking subjects into geometric forms, so is one kind of artist.

clue.text: In time, liberal turned up, contributing to unity

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: turned up in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: large can mean generous or liberal, as in large-hearted

explanation.surface: Eventually a free thinker arrived, helping to unite.
explanation.definitionFit: Something integral is essential to the whole, so it contributes to making a unity.

clue.text: Invert open vessel

parts.note: overt means open, not hidden
an urn is a vessel or vase

explanation.surface: Turn upside down an uncovered container.
explanation.definitionFit: To invert something is to turn it upside down, the same as to overturn it.

clue.text: Disease reduced by exactly 50% in one area, part of Europe

indicators.note: in signals the shortened disease sitting inside the letters for one and area

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: cutting the disease's name precisely in half keeps one of its two identical halves

parts.note: beriberi is a disease caused by lack of vitamin B1

explanation.surface: An illness halved in one region of the continent.
explanation.walkthrough: The disease's name is two identical halves, so cutting it exactly in half is clean; the half sits between the letters for one and area.
explanation.definitionFit: Iberia is the peninsula holding Spain and Portugal, a region of south-west Europe.

clue.text: Repackaged into new aid for all of us

indicators.note: something repackaged is put together again in a new form, so the letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: Fresh aid is rebundled for everyone's benefit.
explanation.definitionFit: Something nationwide extends across the whole country, so it covers every one of us citizens.

clue.text: Nut or vegetable

definitions.meaning: nut and ... are both slang for the head
the broad ... or runner ... is a vegetable

explanation.definitionFit: Bean is slang for the head, as is nut, and a bean is also a common pulse vegetable.

clue.text: Geometrical instrument for vehicle

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of
a tractor is a farm vehicle

explanation.surface: A drawing tool suited to a farm machine.
explanation.definitionFit: A protractor is the semicircular tool used in geometry for measuring angles.

clue.text: Request presented, with no clear leader in tournament

definitions.text: Request presented, with no clear leader
definitions.meaning: a petition whose signatures are written in a circle so that no one appears to head the list
a competition in which each player meets every other in turn

explanation.surface: A petition was submitted, but nobody led the event.
explanation.definitionFit: A round robin is both a circularly signed petition hiding its instigator and an all-play-all competition.

clue.text: Easy task, as opposed to adult's work

definitions.meaning: a job that takes no effort at all
the play of a youngster, set against grown-ups' labour

explanation.definitionFit: Child's play is an idiom for something very easy, and literally the playing a youngster does instead of work.

clue.text: Inspiring activity around time of entertaining spectacle

indicators.note: around tells us the breathing word goes round the period of time

parts.note: a pant is a breath taken in, literally inspiration of air
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: Uplifting work surrounding the period of a grand show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inspiring' looks like 'uplifting' but means breathing in, so the activity is a PANT.
explanation.definitionFit: A pageant is a lavish public show or procession staged to entertain spectators.

clue.text: Island between river banks in French city

parts.note: the Po is the longest river in Italy
tiers are rows or banks, as of seats

explanation.surface: An isle lies between the edges of a stream in a city in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banks' looks like the river's sides, but it is TIERS, rows of seating; 'between' is only a link here.
explanation.definitionFit: Poitiers is a historic city in west-central France, site of a famous 1356 battle.

clue.text: US claim falsified in Oklahoma, say

indicators.note: falsified suggests the words are altered from their true form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An American assertion turned out untrue in an American state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'falsified' rearranges US CLAIM. 'Oklahoma' poses as the state but is the Rodgers and Hammerstein stage show.
explanation.definitionFit: Oklahoma! is a famous stage musical, so it is an example of the genre.

clue.text: Less than admirable character I put in another novel

indicators.note: put in means placed inside, so the single letter goes into the rearranged word
novel means new, so the word appears in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A dubious protagonist I place in yet another book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' rearranges ANOTHER to ANTHERO, and 'put in' places I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An antihero is a central character lacking conventional heroic virtues, hence less than admirable.

clue.text: Provider of bouquet primate wrapped in pink paper

indicators.note: wrapped in means enclosed by, so the animal sits within the newspaper

parts.note: the Financial Times, FT, is printed on pink paper
a loris is a small nocturnal primate

explanation.surface: Someone supplying flowers has a monkey wrapped in pink newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: The FT, the London Financial Times, is famous for its salmon-pink pages. 'bouquet' also suggests a wine's aroma.
explanation.definitionFit: A florist sells and arranges flowers, so supplies bouquets.

clue.text: Recorded agreement with two or three nominal reductions?

definitions.meaning: signing a document with one's initials records that one agrees to it

definitions.text: with two or three nominal reductions?
definitions.meaning: a name cut down to its first letters, two or three of them, is a set of initials

explanation.definitionFit: Initialling a document marks agreement, and the marks used are initials, names reduced to their first letters.

clue.text: Acting dead? On the contrary

definitions.meaning: a ball that is dead is out of play, so the opposite is still live in the game

explanation.definitionFit: In play means both performing in a staged drama and, of a ball, still live in the game.

clue.text: Facts somewhat back-to front

indicators.note: back to front tells us the phrase for somewhat is written in reverse order

parts.note: a tad means a little, somewhat

explanation.surface: Information that is partly the wrong way round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somewhat' looks like it signals part of a word, but it is A TAD, which 'back-to front' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: Data are facts and figures collected for reference or analysis.

clue.text: Theatrical entrepreneur and I confounded Paris and Rome

indicators.note: confounded means thrown into confusion, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A showman and I got muddled between two European capitals.
explanation.definitionFit: An impresario organises and finances theatrical productions or concerts, a business figure of the stage.

clue.text: Greatly amused a lot of Americans

definitions.meaning: an informal past tense: to kill someone with laughter is to amuse them hugely
an American informal word for a large number or quantity

explanation.definitionFit: Slew is the past of slay, slang for amusing hugely, and in the US a slew is a large amount.

clue.text: Less shy as bachelor, having gained maturity

parts.note: someone who has gained maturity has grown older

explanation.surface: A single man is more confident now that he has grown up.
explanation.definitionFit: Bolder means more daring or confident, the opposite of shyer.

clue.text: Test again concerning dunces before end of class

parts.note: re means concerning, about
asses are fools, dunces

indicators.note: end of picks out the final letter of the word class

explanation.surface: Examine the slow learners once more before the lesson finishes.
explanation.definitionFit: To reassess is to evaluate or examine again, a fresh test of something.

clue.text: Poet from New York so accepted by Southern state

indicators.note: accepted by means taken inside, so the state's letters enclose the others

parts.note: Tenn is the abbreviation for Tennessee, a southern US state
taken as written

explanation.surface: A versifier from New York is welcomed by a Southern state.
explanation.walkthrough: The state's abbreviation is split so the inserted letters go between its two Ns; 'Southern state' in the US means one of the old South.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred, Lord Tennyson was a Victorian poet laureate, so he is an example of a poet.
